Welcome to the course EE639 Lasers!
Lasers have changed our lives in ways that could scarcely have been imagined a few decades back. Lasers
shape the way we communicate at mind-boggling speeds through optical fibers, help to perform industrial-
grade cutting and machining with unprecedented precision and speed, are used to perform bloodless
surgery of the highest complexity, are helping to “see” the firing of neurons inside the brain, are used to
build extremely small biochemical sensors, are used to detect gravitational waves, provide ultra-stable
navigational tools and a huge range of other applications.
The overall objective of the course is to introduce the student to the world of lasers through a mixture of
lectures, demonstrations, assignments and industrial visits. Any student who has studied electronics or
physics would be able to grasp the fundamental processes.
Special attractions of this course:
1. Laboratory-based assignments. You will learn how to operate semiconductor lasers and to
characterize some of their properties in the Photonic Sensors Lab (AB 13/327).
2. Visits to prominent lasers labs in PRL Ahmedabad: You will visit renowned laser labs in PRL where
ultrafast lasers spanning laser wavelength ranges are developed.
3. Guest lectures be experts: Several eminent experts from India and abroad will be invited to deliver
lectures on different applications of lasers. This will give you a clearer and a more up to date picture
of the landscape of lasers.
Some FAQs:
Q1: Does this course involve heavy mathematics or is the emphasis more on concepts?
A : The emphasis will always be on the concepts. The mathematics is used to provide insights into the
details. It is more important to understand the concepts on which the laser is built. These concepts are
actually very simple ones and the student typically comes across them in many other branches of science
and engineering.
Q3: I did not study physics in great depth in my UG course? Would I be able to do this course?
A : Yes, you will be able to understand lasers if you understand simple harmonic motion, time constants,
feedback, oscillators, basic semiconductor physics (electrons and holes), and simple differential equations.
One of the aims of the course is to show that the same concepts that are taught in electronics are applicable
with almost no change in the field of photonics.
Q4: I have always been scared of electromagnetic waves. Do I have any chance in this course?
A : EM waves are usually not taught well in most UG colleges. Dont take this course if you understand
absolutely nothing of EM waves. You will have no difficulty in this course if you have done an undergraduate
course in EM waves even if you have forgotten many topics.
Q5: I have never studied quantum mechanics. Would I be able to do this course?
A : The amount of quantum mechanics in this course is not significant. It is also included for the sake of
completeness. It is included so that the story of the laser can be told in a more coherent way. Dont worry
if you do not understand it - an uneasy feeling can often be useful.
Q6: I have never done any optics experiments. How would I be able to work in the lab?
A : You will work under the supervision of PhD students. You will mostly use fiber-optic components that
are connected in much the same way as the BNC cables that you have used in electronics labs. The lab
sessions will help some of the ideas to sink in.
Q7: Can I take this course as an ES course?
A : This is an elective course that EE offers to BTech, MTech and PhD students. The course can be taken as
an EE discipline-specific elective or as an ES course.

Course contents:
Fundamental wave and quantum properties of light, light-matter interaction;, discrete energy levels;
Radiative transitions and emission line width, energy levels and radiative properties of matter, radiation
and thermal equilibrium; Absorption and stimulated emission, population inversion, gain and gain
saturation, laser oscillation above threshold, population inversion requirements in 2-, 3-and 4-level
systems, laser pumping; Laser resonators, stable resonators, Gaussian beams, special cavities; Specific
laser systems, solid-state lasers, pulsed lasers; Semiconductor lasers, edge-emitting and surface emitting
lasers, quantum cascade lasers; Modulation of lasers; electro-optic, acousto-optic and direct current
modulation; Frequency multiplication of laser beams, introduction to nonlinear optical effects.

2 Course Content and Modules
The course is centered around Multiple Input Multiple Output-Orthogonal Frequency Division Multiplexing (MIMO-
OFDM),thekeyphysicallayertechniquethatgoesintobuildinga5GNR/WiFiwirelessnetwork. Thecourseisbroken
downintothefollowingmodules:
1. BackgroundandPreliminaries(Weeks1-2): RelevantbasicsofSignalsandSystems,andCommunicationSys-
tems,LinearAlgebra,andProbability.
2. OFDMinAWGNChannels(Weeks2-3): Comparisonwithconventionalfrequencydivisionmultiplexing(FDM),
orthogonality,relationshiptoFastFourierTransform(FFT)andInverseFFT(IFFT),basicOFDMtransceiver,Bit
ErrorRate(BER)analysisinAdditiveWhiteGaussianNoise(AWGN)Channels.
3. SISO Wireless Channels (Weeks 4-5): Large-scale fading phenomena (shadowing, pathloss, etc.), small-scale
fadingphenomena(multipath,Doppler),RayleighandRicianFading,Jakeschannelmodel,Wide-SenseStationary
UncorrelatedScattering(WSSUS)model,Single-input-single-output(SISO)wirelesschannelmodel.
4. SISO-OFDMDesignandPerformance(Weeks6-7): Inter-SymbolInterference(ISI),Zero-Padding/CyclicPre-
fix (CP), Inter-Carrier Interference (ICI), SISO-OFDM BER Performance in Rayleigh fading channels, Peak-to-
AveragePowerRatio(PAPR).
5. SISO-OFDMSignalProcessing(Weeks7-8): SynchronizationusingSchmidl-CoxMethod,ChannelEstimation,
Equalization.
6. MIMO Wireless Channel Models (Weeks 9-10): Angle-of-Arrival (AoA), Angle-of-Departure (AoD), Spatial
Correlationandexamples,Multiple-input-multiple-output-OFDM(MIMO-OFDM)channelmodel,channelmatrix,
channelstateinformation(CSI).
7. MIMO-OFDM Techniques (Weeks 10-12): Diversity, Multiplexing, Diversity-Multiplexing Tradeoff (DMT),
MassiveMIMO.
8. Puttingitalltogether(Week13): In-classdemoofend-to-endMIMO-OFDMsystem.

High Frequency Engineering
Course contents
Introduction - High Frequency, Frequency range, RF, Microwave, MM wave and Tera Hertz, Concept of
Insertion-phase and Transit-time, Their Significance, Features , applications;
High Frequency Network Representations - Various matrix representations, Z, Y, h, ABCD Matrix,
Scattering Matrix, Generalized Scattering Matrix, Shifting of Reference Plane Properties, Different
Matrix Conversions;
Passive Circuits Design – Definition of Coupling Co-efficient, Isolation, Directivity, Power Divider,
Power Combiner, Directional Couplers, Design of Hybrid, Rat-Race, Backward-wave Couplers,
Different Filter Design;
Amplifier and Oscillator Design - Transistor’s Scattering Matrix Representation, Definition of various
Gains, Stability Criteria/Circles, Unilateral case, Figure of Merit, Constant Gain Circles, Definition of
Noise, Design of Low Noise Amplifier, One port Oscillator design;
Introduction to High Frequency Systems- - Wireless Link design, Radar, Parameters, Radar Equations.

Learning outcomes
This course deals with basic concepts of high frequency circuit design and will lead to followings:
• Skill development of high frequency circuit design which will be useful in R&D and Industry. Students
will be able to design and analyze microwave circuits both passive and active.
• Capability to design RF components, fabricate and test their performance
• Provide exposure to RF system design
• Lead to furtherance of concepts of wave/transmission line theory
• Supplement to the curriculum of VLSI/Embedded System; particularly the RFIC design
• Facilitate solving signal integrity / EMI_EMC issues
